text: hey everybody why did the overwhelming majority of biblical Scholars agree that the Pastoral Epistles so that would be first and second Timothy and Titus were
not written by Paul but were written decades after his death there are a number of considerations that point in this direction and I'm
going to divide them into external evidence linguistic data and thematic considerations
regarding external evidence we have pretty clear indications that their authenticity was doubted by many not by
all but by many in the earliest periods of Christianity Jerome for instance says that the second century Christian
theologianation who put together an early Harmony of the gospels accepted the authenticity of Titus but rejected the authenticity of first and second
Timothy we have Martian's gospel which includes the entire Pauline Corpus except for Hebrews and the Pastoral
Epistles one of our earliest actual witnesses to the Pastoral Epistles as a collection Chester Beatty's p-46 omits
the Pastoral Epistles and one of our earliest witnesses to the New Testament as a whole codex vaticanus also omits
the Pastoral Epistles we've also got linguistic data of the 850 or so Greek words that occur within
the Pastoral Epistles and this is not including personal or place names a full one-third of them do not appear in any
of the other Pauline Epistles and of that one-third the majority are actually quite common to Hellenistic literature
from the late first century CE in the early 2nd Century CE including a lot of Christian writings from that time period
after the death of Paul from a thematic point of view there are divergences within the Pastoral Epistles
Paul's focus on the Soma the body is completely absent from the Pastoral Epistles Paul's notion of the time being
short this expectation that Jesus would be back soon is absent from the Pastoral Epistles Paul's notion of righteousness
is different in the Pastoral Epistles Paul's notion of being in Christ is different in the Pastoral Epistles
Paul's notion of the relationship of Faith to works is different in the Pastoral Epistles the Pastoral Epistles
are also focused on establishing pastoral or administrative Frameworks
for the life of the church and these concerns are far more developed than they were in the other Pauline Epistles
suggesting this is taking place when the Christian church is more established and more developed and is looking to more
long-term administrative concerns so all of these considerations combine to convince the overwhelming majority of
biblical Scholars that the Pastoral Epistles were not written by Paul but were composed decades after his death either toward the end of the first
century CE or in the opening years of the second century CE
